solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grounded for messing about, he's no favourite

indicators.note: messing about with something jumbles it, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is confined to their room for fooling around and is clearly out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounded' looks like the start of a story about punishment, but it is the fodder for 'messing about'.
explanation.definitionFit: The contestant not expected to win is the opposite of the favourite in betting terms.

clue.text: Cheap paper's report of recognised race

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: recognised is knew and a race is a sprint, together knew sprint

explanation.surface: A tabloid writes up a well-known race on poor paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap, low-grade paper that newspapers are printed on.

clue.text: Prepare to defend yourself from dreadful anger from across the Channel

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the word is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: de is French for from, French being the language across the Channel

explanation.surface: A warning to brace yourself against terrible rage coming from France.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call to take up a defensive stance before a bout.

clue.text: The spirit of March and November

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something capturing the essence of two months of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' and 'November' look like months; one is a protest march, the other the radio code word for N.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit or devil.

clue.text: Golf balls in sludge perhaps

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is a round letter, like a ball, so two balls give two Os

explanation.surface: Golf balls end up lost in a muddy bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is any sticky or slimy substance, and sludge is one example.

clue.text: Shot round on eastern motorway, one getting circulation problems

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the turned shot follows the first two letters

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for the shot is read backwards

parts.note: a lob is a high shot in tennis
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gunshot on a motorway in the east leaves someone with problems in the blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire; it is a tennis lob, and 'on' places it after the eastern motorway letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Emboli are clots or air bubbles blocking blood vessels, which disrupt the circulation.

clue.text: Person in capital has endless comfort and cash, say

indicators.note: endless means the word for comfort loses its last letter

parts.note: ease is comfort
cash is an example of legal tender, money that must be accepted

explanation.surface: A city dweller enjoys unending comfort and money.
explanation.walkthrough: An East Ender is a Londoner from the East End, London being the capital. 'endless' cuts EASE to EAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from London's East End lives in the British capital.

clue.text: Saving income? What to buy if so

parts.note: saving as a preposition means except, as does bar
income is gain, money coming in

explanation.surface: A question about putting money aside, with advice on what to purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to 'Saving': a good buy is something to purchase if you want to save money.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase made cheaply is a good deal, the thing a thrifty shopper should snap up.

clue.text: Boozer encouraging weight loss

definitions.meaning: boozer is British slang for a pub, here the nearest one to your home

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker trying to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' suggests a drinker; in British slang it is the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Your local is the pub nearest your home; lo-cal food is low in calories.

clue.text: Singer's beginning to shake booty

indicators.note: the beginning of the word Singer is its first letter

parts.note: to wag is to shake to and fro, as a dog its tail

explanation.surface: A pop singer starts the show by shaking her bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booty' reads as slang for buttocks; here it means plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for stolen goods, the loot or plunder of a robbery.

clue.text: Deranged Poles boarding low vehicle

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the poles go inside the other pieces

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
a truck is a goods vehicle
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Mad Polish passengers climb aboard a lorry that rides low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' tempts as nationality; it is the two magnetic poles, north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstruck once meant driven mad by the moon, hence crazed or unhinged.

clue.text: Program with right allure for learner

parts.note: an app is a computer program
to allure is to entice or tempt

explanation.surface: A piece of software with the right appeal for someone learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee bound to a master to learn a trade is a learner of that craft.

clue.text: Soldier overturned sort of gas in base

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the soldier is turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a noble gas is one of the inert gases such as neon

explanation.surface: A soldier is knocked over by a gas at an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military base; it is the adjective meaning low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base as an adjective means morally low, dishonourable.

clue.text: Completely unknown bedfellow

parts.note: all as an adverb means completely
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A sleeping partner nobody knows anything about.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfellow is used figuratively for a partner or associate, as in strange bedfellows in politics.

clue.text: With film not starting, writer's yawning

indicators.note: not starting means the word for film loses its first letter

parts.note: a video is a recorded film
a pen is a writer; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A writer yawns when the film fails to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the V from VIDEO, leaving IDEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawning gap or chasm is one gaping wide, fully unclosed.

clue.text: Planned a trip, ready to ditch English Heritage

indicators.note: planned means arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

indicators.note: to ditch means to drop, so the letter for English is removed

parts.note: ready is British slang for cash, as in the ready

explanation.surface: An outing to an English Heritage site is planned, ready to go.
explanation.walkthrough: English Heritage is a body caring for historic sites in England, but here the words split. 'Planned' rearranges A TRIP; 'to ditch' takes E from MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrimony is property inherited from one's father or ancestors, a heritage.

clue.text: Depressed little Edward goes backwards — and forwards

indicators.note: goes backwards means the short form of Edward is read in reverse

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward
and forwards supplies the other pet form of Edward, Ted, read the normal way

explanation.surface: Young Edward is feeling low and rocks to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pet names of Edward are used: NED turned by 'goes backwards' gives DEN, then TED read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something depressed has been pushed in, leaving a hollow in its surface.

clue.text: Forced out old media boss

parts.note: ex means former or old
the press is the news media
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A former newspaper chief was pushed out of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice expressed from fruit has been squeezed or pressed out of it.

clue.text: Hard stone urn is cut evenly

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

indicators.note: evenly means taking the even-numbered letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A tough stone urn has been carved with a regular pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight. 'evenly' takes letters 2, 4, 6 and 8 of 'urn is cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict teacher or rule is hard, severe and unyielding.

clue.text: Covered small hardened cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the word for hardened wraps the small letter

parts.note: inured means hardened or accustomed to hardship

explanation.surface: Small toughened containers are protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Being covered by a policy means being protected against loss.

clue.text: Seize back and sharply strike hospital chart

indicators.note: back means the word for seize is turned round

parts.note: to grab is to seize
a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: Someone grabs and slaps a hospital patient's chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar graph is a diagram showing quantities as columns, a kind of chart.

clue.text: Arguments are involved with issue

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as sons

explanation.surface: Disputes get tangled up over a contested matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a topic of debate; it is offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds or justifications given in a debate are its arguments.

clue.text: The burden borne by The Times

parts.note: something borne by a person rests on them
the newspaper speaks of itself as us, so the paper itself means us

explanation.surface: The newspaper carries the weight of responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the paper this clue appears in, so it refers to itself as 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus means a duty or responsibility that has to be carried.

clue.text: What's in vase returned for statesman

indicators.note: in means the interjection is placed inside the other piece
returned in a down clue means the vessel is read upwards

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase
eh is an interjection meaning what; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A question about what is inside a vase sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Nehru led India to independence and became its first prime minister, a famous statesman.

clue.text: Ship rocks, vessel going around river

parts.note: a drink on the rocks is served with ice

indicators.note: going around means the vessel surrounds the letter for river

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A ship hits rocks and a boat circles round a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks nautical, but it is ice, as in whisky on the rocks; 'vessel' is a cup, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a strengthened ship that cuts channels through frozen seas.

clue.text: What hatchback and Cadillac do with black frost announced

indicators.note: announced means said aloud, so the word for frost is heard

parts.note: rime is a kind of frost, frozen fog on surfaces

explanation.surface: Two cars in a cold snap, one black with frost.
explanation.walkthrough: Hatchback and Cadillac end in the same sound, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Words whose endings sound alike, as these two car words do, are said to chime that way.

clue.text: Careful to dress Italian lady in white

indicators.note: to dress means to clothe, so the word for careful wraps the Italian lady

parts.note: chary means cautious or careful
donna is Italian for lady

explanation.surface: A cautious person dresses an Italian woman all in white.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a grape and the wine made from it, among the best-known white wines.

clue.text: Score half as many from the back

indicators.note: from the back means the number is read backwards, upwards in this down clue

parts.note: half a score of twenty is ten

explanation.surface: Score half as many points from the back of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' does double duty in the surface: as the definition it is to net a goal, while 'half as many' plays on a score being twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: To net is to score a goal, putting the ball into the net.

clue.text: Dismiss leader going AWOL in mounted combat

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and going absent means it is removed

parts.note: a joust is combat between knights on horseback

explanation.surface: A commander is sacked after his officer deserts in a cavalry fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to drive out or remove someone from a post.

clue.text: Naturally remove moisture from divers

definitions.meaning: to dry something in the open by the heat of the sun
divers is an old word for several or various

explanation.surface: Sunshine dries off people who have been swimming underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is the adjective meaning various, not people who dive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or miscellaneous, matching the old adjective divers.

clue.text: Industrial region's seediest vagrant

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters of the word wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A down-at-heel tramp hangs about the grimiest industrial area.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition is read as 'is', joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesside is the industrial area around the River Tees in north-east England, known for steel and chemicals.
